text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- Leaders of coalition Zajedno appeal for restraint after crowds shatter windows of Serbian television and newspaper publishing house Politika buildings, say will bring in more party orderlies to prevent provocations.
- Coalition Zajedno says it does not recognise third round of local elections.
- Patriarch Pavle of the Serbian Orthodox Church appeals for acceptance of the will of the people.
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic receives Cyrus Vance, head of U.N. delegation for missing persons on the territory of former Yugoslavia.
- Serbian government adopts document on 1997 economic policy.
- "What Serbia needs above all is internal stability," Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic says after voting in third round of local elections in Belgrade.
- Bosnian Serb parliament elects new government headed by Prime Minister Gojko Klickovic.

- Serbian deputy prime minister and agriculture minister Nedeljko Sipovac says there is enough wheat from this year's crop to meet domestic demand if it is used rationally, imports of wheat and flour will stabilise the market.
- Firm dinar exchange rate achieved solely through economic measures, money supply strictly controlled, says National Bank of Yugoslavia deputy governor Bozidar Gazivoda.
- Ljubisa Ristic, president of Yugoslav Left, says the left will not lead people into the streets but will insist that problems be resolved in parliaments.

- Politika newspaper house announces it will raise criminal charges for damage caused to its premises by opposition demonstrators, estimated at several million dinars. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
